title: Kth Largest Score
summary: Track the k-th highest score on a live leaderboard as new scores arrive.

stages.title: Kth largest
stages.requirement:
A leaderboard shows the score needed to make the top `k`. Implement `KthLargest(k, scores)`,
where `scores` is the initial list (maybe empty), and `add(score)`, which records a score and
returns the **k-th largest** score seen so far, counting duplicates. If fewer than `k`
scores have been seen, return `None`. `k >= 1`.

```python
board = KthLargest(3, [4, 5, 8, 2])
board.add(3)   # -> 4
board.add(5)   # -> 5
board.add(10)  # -> 5
board.add(9)   # -> 8
```

Up to 100,000 `add` calls.

hints: You only ever need the top k scores, not all of them.
Keep a min-heap of size at most k. Its root is the k-th largest. Push the new score and pop the smallest when the heap exceeds k.

solution.explanation:
A min-heap holding the k largest scores has the k-th largest at its root. New scores
replace the root only when they beat it (`heapreplace`, O(log k)). Before k scores
exist there is no k-th largest, so we return `None`.
